statements.statement: Both papers B and C emphasize the use of mid-level representations and simulation environments to facilitate autonomous driving training and testing.

Paper B describes ChauffeurNet as an RNN that takes mid-level input and outputs driving trajectories, enabling training on real or simulated data and closed-loop simulation testing before real deployment.

Paper C presents CARLA as an open-source simulator supporting development, training, and validation of autonomous urban driving systems, providing flexible sensor suite specification and environmental conditions, and enabling controlled scenario evaluation.
This theme highlights the shared focus on mid-level input representations and simulation platforms to advance autonomous driving research and deployment.

parsed.type_evidence: Claims 1, 2, 3 (mid-level representations and simulation in Paper B) and claims 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 (simulation platform in Paper C)
